take_homes: The model re-reads the whole conversation every time, so what I put in front changes the answer. I can test that myself in two minutes.
The agent flatters its own work when it reviews it. Treat its report as a claim, check it against what I saw, and get a cold reader if it matters.
Lessons can be saved as a plain rules file that the next session reads.

monday.move: Try the Italy/Finland dinner test in two chat windows, then run one real work document through the 'name three generic claims' check on a fresh session. Nothing more unless it shows a real difference.
monday.when: Tuesday morning, 20 minutes between steering groups
monday.stop_condition: The output looks the same with and without context, or the check finds nothing I would not have found myself.
monday.blocker: The steering-group calendar, and not knowing whether our company data is allowed in the tool.

misconception.why: The module said plainly that the tool grades itself too kindly and showed how to check it. That candour about a limit is what I look for. The filler paragraphs did the opposite. They are the same wait-and-see material I expected, so I am only shaken, not changed.

one_line: The exercises were real and honest about what does not work. The 'Note on context' paragraphs are the same slide I saw in agile, digital and OKRs, and they should be cut.
